strings.en:
In a gambit to learn more about their mysterious pursuers, the king and his mesmer escort, tired and tattered, had set a trap for a mursaat who had wandered further ahead of their hunting party. On their own, a single mursaat was formidable—deadly, but not invincible. Even with their foe defeated, one of Gauvain's students fell in the skirmish and King Jadon sustained serious injuries attempting to protect the young spell-slinger. The rest attempted to carry the king afterward, but he would succumb to his wounds the following day.  
  
The remaining four continued into South Kessex, toward what King Jadon thought could be a possible safe haven. During their detour to "bury" the dead, the mursaat had made up for lost ground and would eventually surround them. The duchess and her comrades stared down their attackers as the Veil of Ilya revealed their presence once more. In a blinding moment of flashing sigils and spellcraft, the four were dazed by the light—only to find the mursaat lying dead around them.  
  
Before them appeared the projection of a man who introduced himself as Obryn—a seemingly powerful spellcaster in his own right. Their mysterious savior would help them find proper shelter near the village of Shaemoor and keep them informed as best he could.

### Shadow & the Quartermaster
The cascading drool of Shadow's slobbery welcome twinkled on Leo's nose.

"See! He's a delight!" screeched Tinker.

"'Course I am! 'Course I am!" barked Shadow. "And now I'm an honorary kitty too, right? Right, Tinker? Always wanted to be!"

"No!" hissed everyone except Leo.

"Fine," growled Leo, holding up a paw. "I'll brook no argument! I am the captain, after all!"

"What am I?" whimpered Shadow. "What do I do? What's my job? If I don't have a job, Master Kae says—"

"Master... Yes, that's it! You'll be the master-at-arms!" yowled Leo, pleased with himself.

"Speaking of masters, we'll need a quartermaster, too, right?" asked Shenanigans. "Sadie's always getting pets from those robed people wandering in the ravine below her territory. And quarters are like shelters on a boat, right?"

Leo agreed this logic was infallible, and the crew began their long trek to the opposite corner of the strand.

In the limitless reaches of the Fractals of the Mists, it is not impossible that you should run into yourself. It could be a nearly identical copy, an evil double, or a version of you that made a different decision at some critical juncture in your life!

If you find yourself meeting yourself, take a deep breath, and keep a few key points in mind:
- Do not engage yourself in conversation, especially about the differences in your lives.
- Do not fight with yourself! This can lead to lingering nightmares and trauma.
- Attempt to exit the encounter and fractal without extended exposure to the copy.
- Upon your return to Tyria, be sure to mention the encounter in your report, and attend a clone-screening session. (See Consortium Troubleshooter's Manual, Section 14.)

While I am labeling these field reports with 90%% certainty as to the accuracy of the numbering, I do recognize the optimism one must apply to view these as "field reports." I do what I must to stave off the further erosion of my spirits.  
  
After escaping the "rabble"—wait, I suppose I should cover that first.  
  
Ignaxious's assertion that they would find me adequate dinner fare was thankfully erroneous. Embarrassingly, I believe they even mistook me for one of their kind at first. From a distance, assuredly, as this seems an impossible (and highly offensive) mix-up to me. But it is one that I'm grateful for, nonetheless.  
  
So, after cleaning myself of slobber and engaging in polite—if hard to follow—conversation, I skirted my way along the land's edge in an attempt to steer clear of both physical and mental probes and continue my mission of gathering intel. My hope is that if and when the Lady Peitha's invasion begins, these field reports will be discovered and put to some use.  
  
Granted, they've only served to document my own self-centered tribulations thus far. Given that they will likely end up as low Kryptis excrement, my disappointment in myself is less than it might otherwise be.  
  
—Operative Selly
